thread.title: Apple Loop: Massive iPhone 11 Leaks, Tim Cook's Big Battery Problem, iPhone XR Price Cuts

author: Ewan Spence
title: Apple Loop: Massive iPhone 11 Leaks, Tim Cook's Big Battery Problem, iPhone XR Price Cuts
text:
Taking a look back at another week of news and headlines from Cupertino, this week’s Apple Loop includes three new features for the iPhone 11, more price cuts for the iPhone XR, how many batteries Apple replaced, USB-C on your new iPhone, some bedtime reading from Qualcomm, the surprising future for AirPower, and the smart battery case returns. Apple Loop is here to remind you of a few of the very many discussions that have happened around Apple over the last seven days ( and you can read my weekly digest of Android news here on Forbes ).
ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT Three New Features For the iPhone XI
Following an investors report, some of the additional features for the iPhone family for the 2019 handsets have been revealed: a new antenna, improved WiFi, and a brighter light for facial recognition. Are these new features going to be enough to sell the 2019 iPhones in September? Forbes’ Gordon Kelly investigates :
 …Apple is understood to be enhancing Face ID on the iPhone XI by increasing the power of the flood illuminator. This Face ID component beams out infrared (IR) light to illuminate your face ahead of a dot projector firing 30,000 dots of invisible IR to map your face in three dimensions. Improve the illumination and the dot projector can be both faster and more accurate.
More here on Forbes .
Apple CEO Tim Cook presents new products, including new Macbook laptops, during a special event at the Brooklyn Academy of Music (Photo: Timothy A. Clary/AFP/Getty Images) Getty
More Price Cuts Expected For iPhone XR
But the biggest change in the iPhone line up could be a significant price cut on the iPhone XR. With sales of all three 2018 handsets contributing to Apple’s profit warning earlier this month, analysts are predicting that the cuts to carrier subsidies will be followed by larger price cuts in the months to follow - and those cuts will be seen by consumers. Ben Lovejoy reports :
A report that Apple would be rolling out iPhone price cuts across a range of models in China was also confirmed this month, with discounts of around 20% across the iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus and XR.
The price cuts follow Apple’s warning that its earnings for the holiday quarter will be anywhere from $5B to $9B lower than the company originally forecast. The resulting shock has seen AAPL shares plunge further and analysts reduce their target price for the stock.
More details and discussion on 9to5Mac .
Battery Replacements And Anticipating Problems
ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT How much of an impact did Apple’s battery replacement program have on sales of the iPhone XR, XS, and XS Max (which lead to the profit warning earlier this month)? As John Gruber notes , Apple anticipated 1-2 million battery replacements in a normal year, but saw 11 million under the replacement program:
… even if it was more popular than Apple originally expected, why wasn’t it accounted for in guidance issued on November 1 — 10 months after the program started? My guess: the effect of the battery replacement program on new iPhone sales wasn’t apparent until after the iPhone XR and XS models were available. A few million extra iPhone users happy with the performance of their old iPhones with new batteries — who would have otherwise upgraded to a new iPhone this year — put a ding in the bottom line.
And that is a question that lies at the heart of Apple’s profit warning. All the signs were there that something was going to go wrong, and none of them were picked up.
USB-C iPhone
While the jury seems to be out on USB-C replacing Lightning in the new iPhones, it would be remiss to not talk about it, especially as the iPad Pro has already made the jump. Macotakara has more :
ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT In addition, similar to iPad Pro 11-inch, iPad Pro 12.9-inch (3rd generation), next iPhone might also employ USB-C connector. However, those who are working on it said that it has not reached reference step, and if microUSB connector is continued to be employed has not been decided yet.
TechRadar’s Matt Swider isn’t so sure :
USB-C has been predicted for the iPhone 11. "We have a different information," says CompareRaja via notable smartphone leaker Steve Hemmerstoffer. This particular iPhone prototype is said to show a traditional Lightning connection.
Of course, between now and the expected iPhone 11 launch in eight months, Apple could start using USB-C. Also, since the company is expected to have three new iPhones for 2019, we could see more more advanced models, like the iPhone 11 Max, get USB-C.
More at TechRadar .

Bedtime Reading From Qualcomm Court Case
With witnesses from Apple, Samsung and Ericsson, the FTC’s case against Qualcomm, alleging it is a monopoly, has thrown up many incidents and case studies from smartphone manufacturing over the last few years involving Apple. Shara Tibken lays out the story so far :
ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT The FTC, aided by chipmaker Intel and iPhone vendor Apple, filed suit two years ago, accusing Qualcomm of forcing customers like Apple to work with it exclusively and charging excessive licensing fees for its technology. The US believes Qualcomm has a monopoly on modem chips and harmed competition by trying to maintain its power. Qualcomm's "excessive" royalty rates prevented rivals from entering the market, drove up the cost of phones and in turn hurt consumers, who faced higher handset prices, the FTC said.
Qualcomm has argued the FTC's lawsuit is based on "flawed legal theory." It's said that customers choose its chips because they're the best and that it has never stopped providing processors to customers, even when they're battling over licenses.
More at CNet .
Here Comes A Surprise…
Is Apple finally ready to improve wireless charging with its AirPower system? If rumors from the production line are correct, the answer is yes. Mike Wuerthele reports :
According to a Tweet from charging watchdogs ChargerLab, mass production of the AirPower has begun at Luxshare Precision.
Luxshare Precision has done a fair amount of Apple's accessory manufacturing for the last decade. Most notably, ChargerLab notes that the company handles some of the AirPods builds, as well as USB-C cabling for Apple. From a historical perspective, ChargerLab has a good track record of predicting when charging accessories will arrive, and who manufactures them.
ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT More at AppleInsider .
Breaking: AirPower is finally coming. We just learned from credible source in supply chain that the manufacture Luxshare Precision has already started producing Apple AirPower wireless charging pad. Luxshare Precision is also the maker of Apple AirPods and USB-C cables. pic.twitter.com/UqgWIAh3sx

And Finally…
Apple’s awkwardly designed battery case (with ‘the hump’) has made its debut for the new XR, XS, and XS Max handsets. Picking up wireless charging capabilities along the way (matching Mophie’s wireless charging cases), they are priced at $129 in the US. Lory Gil reports :
This is more than just an update to fit the latest iPhone. Apple took to heart all our cries of disgust at the Smart Battery Case's "humpback" design and smoothed it out to look like a more traditional battery case.
This year's model also supports Qi wireless charging. So, you can set it and forget it and your case and iPhone will charge at the same time.
More at iMore .
